subject: Tenant slice isolation + deployment runbook — readiness check

Cc: LumenEdge Network Team <netops@lumenedge.com>

Subject: Tenant slice architecture + runbook request

Hi Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Tuesday. As discussed, we're preparing the tenant-slice deployment for our east-coast colo (R1) and need a final runbook and a reference network diagram that separates the control plane tunnels from tenant data paths. A couple of specific asks from NetOps:

- A clear statement on whether control plane traffic will be routed over the customer L3 fabric (BGP) or over an overlay (WireGuard/MTU-encapsulated) 
- Expected SNAT/NAT behavior for tenant egress and if NAT pools are required per-tenant or per-rack
- TLS termination point and cert rotation cadence for control plane mTLS

Could you share a runbook draft and any diagrams you have? If possible, we'd like the initial checklist and a canary plan (small subset of tenants) to review by next Wednesday (2027-11-17).

Sam
Senior SRE, LumenEdge Systems

Attachments: tenant-slice-requirements-LE.pdf (13KB)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-15T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tenant slice architecture + runbook request

Sam — thanks for the clear list. Attaching an initial runbook draft and a flat network map. High level answers up front:

- Control plane: default pattern is to use an overlay (WireGuard tunnels managed by Redwood agent) to ensure control plane traffic is isolated from customer BGP fabric. We can support a routed control plane over BGP for customers who require full convergence into their fabric, but that increases blast radius and requires dedicated route filters.

- Tenant egress NAT: we recommend per-tenant NAT pools scoped to the tenant slice to preserve source fidelity for auditing. Per-rack NAT is possible but complicates cross-tenant tracing and policy enforcement.

- TLS/mTLS: Redwood control plane uses mTLS with certs issued by the customer's KMS-backed CA or Redwood-managed CA depending on contract. Typical rotation cadence is 30 days for ephemeral keys, 90 days for leaf certs (configurable).

See attached: tenant-slice-runbook-v1.pdf and slice-network-flatmap.svg. Soojin has added section on policy enforcement and LFEs (logical function endpoints).

Action: I'll schedule a 45m technical readout on Monday (2027-11-16) to walk the canary checklist. Kimberly — can you confirm whether LumenEdge requested per-tenant NAT pools in the contract addendum?

- Markus
Director, Private Deploys | Redwood Inference

Attachments: tenant-slice-runbook-v1.pdf (1.2MB), slice-network-flatmap.svg (240KB)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant slice architecture + runbook request

Hi Sam — adding the network details Sam asked for and a few operational notes. Key excerpts from the runbook (p.4-7):

1) Control plane overlay behavior
- WireGuard sessions terminate on dedicated control-plane proxies in the MD (management domain). Each proxy has two interfaces: mgmt (customer-facing) and control (internal mTLS). Proxies advertise /32s into the customer BGP fabric only when explicitly requested.
- MTU considerations: overlay adds ~80 bytes. We detect PMTU and will fallback to path MTU discovery; if the colo restricts fragmenting, we fall back to a routed control plane option.

2) Data plane separation
- Tenant data lanes use L2/L3 pinned VLANs per-rack and map to Redwood tenant slices via hardware tags (VLAN tags + VPC VRF). This keeps the fast-path in the customer fabric and avoids double-encapsulation.

3) NAT strategy and observability
- Per-tenant NAT pools recommended. NAT events logged to remote-syslog and pushed to a split-stream to the customer's SIEM and Redwood Observability.
- Audit trail: every NAT allocation includes tenant ID + allocation timestamp + physical host ID.

4) Canary checklist (summary)
- Provision slice in staging with 2 tenants
- Validate control plane handshake over overlay and over BGP (if opted-in)
- Verify egress SNAT with two concurrent flows and confirm audit logs are generated
- Roll traffic to 5% of production tenant load for 2 hours (metrics: p99 latency, token throughput per GPU, net egress delta)

I've dropped a more detailed network flatmap in the drive link Markus listed. Jordan — I'm tagging you for the canary runbook items (traffic shaping, throttles, rollback triggers).

— Soojin
Senior Network Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Sam Patel <sam@lumenedge.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant slice architecture + runbook request

Thanks for the draft — couple of concerns from NetOps after quick review:

- If control plane defaults to overlay, we need a topology diagram showing HA pairs of control proxies and their placement (rack/power domain). Our infra team will not accept black-box proxies without rack-level placement.
- BGP option: we would like a clear failure mode doc that shows what happens to tenant traffic if customer BGP withdraws prefixes for a control proxy. Is there an automatic fallback?
- NAT pools: per-tenant pools are preferred by our security team but they want to know the expected public IP footprint and whether we can pre-allocate on their IP plan.

Can you add the HA placement diagram and a failure-modes appendix to the runbook? Also, please include the canary rollback triggers in the checklist spreadsheet (we need explicit numeric thresholds).

Sam

Subject: Re: Tenant slice architecture + runbook request

Sam — appreciate the fast feedback. We've updated the runbook and checklist per your asks and added a short "failure modes" appendix (see drive link). Summary of changes and next steps:

- HA placement: added explicit placement guidance. Control proxies must be deployed as N+2 across two power domains. Diagram pages 9-11 enumerate rack ids and fallback nodes (attached as slice-network-flatmap.svg and on Drive).
- Failure-mode behavior: if customer BGP withdraws control proxy prefixes, agent heartbeat will flip to a secondary control proxy over the overlay. If both customer fabric and overlay fail, the runtime will enter a read-only mode for model uploads and will serve cached models only; we included automated alerting (PagerDuty) and a fast-rollback path to the prior software image.
- Pre-allocation: Kimberly will coordinate with your IP planning team to reserve a /26 for initial NAT pools (approx 62 usable IPs) and we can grow by /28 increments.
- Canary rollback triggers (added to canary-deploy-checklist.xlsx):
  * p99 latency increase > 40% over baseline for 15 minutes
  * error rate spike > 3% sustained over 5 minutes
  * audit log drop (missing NAT allocations) or loss of heartbeat to >1 control proxy

Action items:
- Kimberly: loop in LumenEdge IP planner and confirm /26 reservation (kimberly_park@redwood.com) — due 2027-11-22
- Jordan: finalize throttles and rollback automation in orchestration (DOCID-78945-CanaryPlan) — due 2027-11-22
- Soojin: add HA placement diagram to page 9 and upload updated SVG — due 2027-11-19 (completed)

I'll run the 45m readout on 2027-11-22 10:00 PT; I'll send a calendar invite with the Drive links and checklist. If anything else comes up before then, reply all.

Thanks — looking forward to the canary.
